label: round 8, phase E — Safari reads <body>, not <html>
notes: Phase D shipped its two colours on <html> and Wil's device pass proved they do nothing: /map declares html #353535 (verified present in the emitted CSS and on the built page) and his address bar still reads #1d1411, the body ground. /map is the only route where the two elements differ enough to tell apart by eye, and it discriminates cleanly — Safari reads <body>, not <html>. Phase A could not have caught this: html and body were BOTH #1d1411 then, so 'the root-background fallback' was indistinguishable from the body fallback, and phase D built on that ambiguity. This is exactly what the client brief's section 1 step 2 says ('otherwise, <body>'s background-color'), so the published source was right and this repo's inference was wrong. FIX: the two phase D rules move from html[...] to html[...] body. That alone would repaint the page, because body's background IS the visible page ground — .sec, .shell, main and section paint nothing, so /map's index section would have gone mid-grey. So the ground is decoupled first: main { background: var(--ground) } paints exactly what body paints today, and <main id="main"> wraps all page content including the footer (verified on the built pages), leaving body's own colour visible only in the bar region and overscroll. CHAPTER PAGES ARE STATIC (Wil, 2026-09-18): the address bar takes the hero brown #100a06 and holds it the whole page. The live section-tracking variant is dropped at his instruction — it needs either the 12px strip phase C3 proved visible, or writing body's colour on scroll, which retints the BOTTOM toolbar too and his brief forbids that on these routes. ACCEPTED COST, and the reason section 9 of the brief says stop and report: body drives rubber-band overscroll at both ends, so overscroll on the five chapter routes goes #1d1411 -> #100a06 and on /map -> #353535, and each route's bottom toolbar takes the same colour as its top. Scrolled chapter pages are unchanged and still composite content through the bar; that is the accepted glass-while-scrolled split from phase A2 and no mechanism reaches it. allowedRoutes stays empty: the ground decoupling must be a visual no-op on all 11 routes, and any drift is a defect to fix rather than a baseline to refresh.
